correctness.rationale: For the Day–James l1 same-sign, l3 opposite-sign plane, coordinate swap is a genuine isometry and averaging Q reduces global optimization to H_t²=(x+y)²+t(x-y)². On same-sign sector R_1=1+t s²; on opposite sector R_3=2^(4/3)(t+u)/(1+3u)^(2/3), logarithmic u derivative (1+u-2t)/[(t+u)(1+3u)]. For 0<t≤1/2, the exact distortion is (1+t)/(2^(4/3)t) up to t=2^(-4/3), and 1+t thereafter. These branches decrease/increase, while t≥1/2 implies D≥1.5, so d_BM²=1+2^(-4/3). Sector boundary xy=0 agrees and the proof covers arbitrary real linear isomorphisms.
